Problem Summary:

### What is changed and how it works?

Proposal: [xxx](url) <!-- REMOVE this line if not applicable -->

What's Changed:
Write the default value(32GB) into mysql.tidb if the cluster is upgraded from 3.0.x to 4.0.
When start tidb-server, check:
1. whether `mem-quota-query` is configured by the user. If so, use the value. If not, goto 2
2. whether the var `mem_quota_query` exists in mysql.tidb. If so, use the value. If not, goto 3.
3. Use the default value(1GB) in 4.0.x.

issue_context.title: keep the default memory-quota-query as before if the tidb cluster is updated from a lower version
issue_context.body:
## Development Task
If a user updates the tidb cluster from a lower version to v4.0.x, the memory-quota-query will be changed from 32GB to 1GB. It may cause a bad influence on the business.

- [x] Set the memory-quota-query default value as 1GB if it's a newly-built cluster
- [x] Keep the memory-quota-query default unchanged if the tidb cluster is updated from a lower version

review_comments: what's the behavior when the `memory-quota-query` config is modified by users? How to know whether the user has modified this config value?
Do not make assumptions, it's better to return the value you read. In case some mistake in writing this value happens, we can discover that soon.

The var in mysql.tidb actually indicates that the cluster was **upgrade from 3.0**.
IMO, even the value is written wrongly, we still need to return 32 << 30.
